# Control Narrative Template for Equipment Modules

## 1. Principle: write the behavior once, document only what differs

Split the narrative into three layers. The integrator writes only layers 2 and 3 per project.

| Layer | Content | Written | Owner | Per-project effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Class narrative** | Everything the library block does: modes, states, commands, feedback monitoring, standard faults, faceplate, default alarms | Once per class and version | Brewery controls engineering | None. Referenced only |
| **2. Instance sheet** | Parameters, I/O, interlocks, alarm setpoints, and who commands the module, as a fixed form or table | One per pump; one row per valve | Integrator, ideally generated from the tag/IO database | Fill in the blanks |
| **3. Deviations** | Behavior that is not in the class | Only if needed | Integrator, approved by the brewery | Ideally zero |

**Rules that stop drift**
1. Instance documents never restate class behavior. They cite it by clause, e.g. `EM-PUMP-VFD v2.1 §5.2`.
2. Every class clause has a stable ID. Clause IDs never get reused, and a revision changes the version.
3. A deviation needs a reason and an approval. If the same deviation appears in a second project, it becomes a library change request.
4. Valves use a table, not paragraphs. Only valves with interlocks beyond the class defaults get a separate instance sheet.
5. Where possible, generate the instance sheet from the same source as the PLC instance data, so document and code can't disagree.

## 2. Layer 1: class narrative skeleton (e.g. `EM-PUMP-VFD`, `EM-PUMP-DOL`, `EM-VALVE-ONOFF`)

| § | Section | Contents (written once) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope and variants | What the class covers, I/O variants (with or without run feedback, VFD, etc.) |
| 2 | Modes | Auto, Manual, Out of Service. Who may command in each mode |
| 3 | States and commands | Stopped, Starting, Running, Stopping, Faulted. Command arbitration, command priority |
| 4 | Permissives and interlocks | How they are evaluated, the difference between *start permissive* and *run interlock (trip)*, latching and reset behavior, bypass handling |
| 5 | Feedback monitoring | Run feedback timeout, unexpected start or stop, VFD ready/fault, speed deviation |
| 6 | Instrument handling | Bad-quality behavior for interlock inputs, shared by all classes |
| 7 | Standard alarms | Alarm list, default priorities, default delays |
| 8 | Parameters | Full parameter table with defaults, ranges, units |
| 9 | HMI faceplate | Layout and operator actions |
| 10 | Standard test script | FAT/SAT steps that apply to every instance |

## 3. Layer 2: instance sheet template

**A. Identification**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tag / description | |
| Area / unit | |
| Class and version | |
| P&ID / drawing | |
| Controlled by (phase/sequence) | |

**B. I/O and hardware**

| Signal | Tag/address | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Run command, run feedback, fault, etc. | | |

**C. Parameters.** List only the parameters the project actually uses. Mark any non-default value.

| Parameter (class §8) | Value | Unit | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|

**D. Interlocks**

| ID | Type (Permissive / Trip) | Source | Condition | Delay | Action | Reset (auto/manual) | Bypassable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**E. Instance-specific alarms.** Include only alarms beyond the class defaults, or defaults with changed setpoints.

**F. Deviations from class.** Write "None" if there are none. Each deviation needs: the clause affected, the behavior required, the reason, and an approval reference.

**G. Instance-specific tests.** Only tests for sections C–F. The class test script covers the rest.

## 4. Worked example: P-4021

> Assumptions to confirm: PT-4022 is on the pump suction, the class name and version are illustrative, and all setpoints and times are placeholders for commissioning. The valve and tank context is not given in your request, so I left it open rather than invent it.

### P-4021 CIP Supply Pump: Instance Sheet

**A. Identification**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Tag / description | P-4021, CIP supply pump |
| Area / unit | CIP |
| Class and version | `EM-PUMP-VFD` v2.1 |
| P&ID | *(to be filled in)* |
| Controlled by | CIP circuit phase (run request and speed setpoint). Manual from HMI in Manual mode |

**B. I/O and hardware**

| Signal | Tag | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Run command / VFD enable | P-4021 | Via VFD, per class §3 |
| Run feedback, VFD ready, VFD fault | P-4021 | Per class §5 |
| Speed setpoint / speed feedback | P-4021 | Scaled 0–100 % |
| Suction pressure | PT-4022 | 4–20 mA, used for dry-run protection (D1, D2) |

**C. Parameters** (all others at class defaults)

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Default? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum speed | 30 | % | No |
| Maximum speed | 100 | % | Yes |
| Ramp up / down | 10 / 10 | s | Yes |
| Run feedback timeout | 5 | s | Yes |
| Speed deviation alarm | 10 % for 15 s | | Yes |

**D. Interlocks**

| ID | Type | Source | Condition | Delay | Action | Reset | Bypassable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Start permissive | PT-4022 | Pressure > 0.3 bar *(placeholder)* | none | Block start; show "Low suction pressure" on faceplate | Auto, when condition clears | No |
| D2 | Trip (dry-run) | PT-4022 | Pressure < 0.15 bar *(placeholder)* | 3 s | Stop pump, latch "Dry-run trip" | **Manual**, only after pressure > D1 level | No (maintenance override per class §4.5, logged) |
| D3 | Trip (instrument) | PT-4022 | Signal bad quality or out of range | 2 s | Treated as D2 (fail-safe) | Manual, after signal healthy | No |

D1 is higher than D2 so there is hysteresis and no chatter at the threshold. D1–D3 follow the class mechanisms in §4 (permissive vs. trip, latching) and §6 (bad quality). This sheet gives only the sources and values.

**E. Instance-specific alarms**

| Alarm | Setpoint | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| P-4021 Dry-run trip | D2 | High (class default for trips) |
| PT-4022 Low pressure warning | 0.25 bar, 5 s *(placeholder)* | Low |

All other alarms (run feedback fail, VFD fault, speed deviation) are class defaults per §7.

**F. Deviations from class**

None.

**G. Instance-specific tests**

| Test | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Simulate PT-4022 below D1 with pump stopped, then command start | Start blocked, faceplate shows reason |
| Run pump, ramp PT-4022 below D2 for longer than 3 s | Pump stops, dry-run trip latched, alarm raised |
| Restore pressure above D1 | Trip stays latched until manual reset, then start is allowed |
| Fail the PT-4022 signal (wire break) | D3 trip as above |
| Command speed below 30 % | Speed clamped to 30 % |

All other tests are executed from the class script (`EM-PUMP-VFD` §10).

## 5. Valves

For the 300 on/off valves, use one table, with the class (`EM-VALVE-ONOFF`) covering all behavior. Fill in one row per valve:

| Tag | Class/ver | Type (single/double solenoid, feedback) | Open/close FB timeout | Failed position | Interlocks (ID → ref) | Deviation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Valves with no interlocks beyond the defaults need no further text. Any valve with a non-trivial interlock gets a section D table like the pump's.

## 6. Rolling this out

1. Write the class narratives from your existing standard library behavior. They should describe what the code already does.
2. Put the instance sheet in a spreadsheet or database with fixed columns, so integrators can't change the structure.
3. State in the integrator spec that a project submission consists of instance sheets plus the deviation list, and nothing else.
4. Review deviations at each project close-out and promote the recurring ones into the next class version.

I can draft the full text of `EM-PUMP-VFD` §3–§7 next if you'd like, or the valve class and its table.
